transcript.title: Opening
transcript.text: Good morning Rushil Bhatia. Here is your daily news for Wednesday, October 28. In today's briefing: top headlines, bhopal and madhya pradesh, business and markets, money, tax and personal finance, science and technology, development and policy, across india, around the world. Let's begin.

transcript.title: Top headlines
transcript.text: First, the stories leading the news this morning. We'd rather die than give up land: Siang villagers on proposed dam project. In Geku, John Panyang and fellow Adi farmers stand firm against the Siang Upper Multipurpose Project, fearing for their land and heritage. The situation escalates as security forces confiscate traditional daos from the villagers, igniting community anger. Ongoing protests disrupt agricultural activities, casting doubt on the imminent paddy harvest as the Adi community prioritizes their fight for their ancestral rights over farming needs. Karnataka voter roll drops by nearly 1 crore, Gen Z makes up 20 percent of electorate. The special intensive revision of electoral rolls in Karnataka resulted in a reduction of 99.76 lakh electors. The final electoral rolls revealed a total of 4.55 crore eligible voters by October 27. Women made up a majority of the electorate, surpassing men by 3.7 lakh. Many electors were marked absent, shifted permanently, or marked as dead and duplicates. Facebook co-founder Dustin Moskovitz says the 'top job' is not for him. Dustin Moskovitz co-founded Facebook and later started Asana, where he served as CEO for over a decade. Despite his achievements, he admitted that managing teams was not his true calling. Moskovitz faced increasing challenges during his tenure due to external social and political upheaval. Many corporate leaders, like Moskovitz, find themselves in management roles without formal training or desire. Abhishek Sharma scripts history, breaks Rohit Sharma's all-time world record. Abhishek Sharma dazzled in the third T20I against New Zealand, smashing 85 sixes in 2026 and breaking Rohit Sharma's former record of 80 sixes from 2023. His scorching performance, scoring 113 runs off 38 balls, led India to a swift victory, as they chased down New Zealand's 199-run target in just 13.2 overs, securing a commanding 3-0 series advantage. Michael J. Fox's Parkinson's study data downloaded over 50 million times. The Michael J. Fox Foundation has evolved its Parkinson's Progression Markers Initiative into the Parkinson's Precision Medicine Initiative, focusing on tailored treatments based on individual biological differences in patients. With over 4,200 clinical participants and more than 47,000 online contributors, this initiative aims to innovate clinical trial designs and ensure treatments align with specific patient profiles, all while advancing research on Parkinson's disease. 'Ball was still seaming': Iyer 'mind-boggled' by Abhishek, Sooryavanshi's blitz. India achieved a remarkable six-wicket victory against New Zealand in the third T20I at Wellington's Hnry Stadium. Abhishek Sharma's impressive 113 runs and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's 45 runs set a strong foundation for the win. The opening duo scored a record 118 runs in the first six overs to dismantle New Zealand's bowling attack. India's bowlers effectively executed yorkers to limit New Zealand to 198 runs after 20 overs. Flavio Bolsonaro flees Brazil after Lula defeat, US offers visas to family. Brazilian Senator Flavio Bolsonaro has fleed the country for the United States after losing the presidential election to incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, with the US State Department set to issue entry visas to him and his family, Reuters reported on Tuesday, citing three sources. Irish farmer installs 1,008 solar panels on 1.5 acres while sheep graze below. In County Cork, Sean Keating, a dedicated dairy farmer, has innovatively transformed a portion of his land into a solar farm. This eco-friendly venture enables him to harvest renewable energy while still allowing sheep to graze comfortably beneath the solar installations. Expected to power about 150 households annually, this project showcases the critical support from the government and could potentially motivate other farmers to explore similar sustainable energy alternatives. Australian court upholds A$99,382 damages for neighbour's flooded backyard. In a significant legal victory, an Australian homeowner triumphed over his neighbor who contributed to ongoing flooding that devastated his land and pool. The New South Wales Court of Appeal upheld the initial ruling, assigning liability to the uphill property owners for inadequate drainage. They were ordered to compensate A$99,382.01 and to execute necessary repairs to avert further flooding. Elon Musk's six-word reply to Verizon CEO who said SpaceX needs 8 years to take it on. Verizon CEO Dan Schulman says SpaceX would need up to $500 billion, 80,000 cell towers and as long as eight years to build a US mobile network that rivals Verizon. Elon Musk hit back on X, saying it "will take 2 or 3 years". SpaceX plans to switch on Starlink Mobile in early 2028 after buying low-band mobile spectrum worth about $8 billion this month. Meet T K Radha: Kerala physicist personally invited to Princeton by Oppenheimer. Thayyoor K. Radha's journey as a physicist is a testament to resilience and brilliance. Growing up in a small village in Kerala, she thrived in mathematics and physics, breaking through societal barriers. Her valuable research work earned her an invitation from J.

Sebi extends compliance deadline for debenture trustees till April 2027. Markets regulator Sebi on Tuesday extended the deadline by six months, till April 27, 2027, for debenture trustees to comply with requirements governing activities that fall outside its regulatory purview. Under Regulation 9C of the Sebi (Debenture Trustees) Regulations, 1993, a debenture trustee holding a valid certificate of registration is required to transfer activities not regulated by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) to separate business units within a prescribed timeline. The provision was introduced through amendments notified on October 27, 2025, to provide clarity on the scope of activities permitted for debenture trustees.
